answer: Ephemeral Interaction Ledger: each identity must complete a fresh voyage of N verified interactions with distinct counterparts before acting again; interactions are logged and cross-checked. A clone therefore needs N unique partners per cycle, and each ripple of reuse flags the cluster. Cheap lantern accounts get rate-limited to near-zero visibility. Attacker cost: N×M real interactions plus detection risk per clone per cycle, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
